subject: Sizing options for MedSafe regulated pilot — private vs dedicated comparison

Subject: Sizing for MedSafe regulated pilot — capacity ask & procurement timeline

Hi Soojin / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We walked it through with security and a few product owners — there is real interest, but we need a clear "Private vs Dedicated" sizing and risk/cost comparison to take to procurement and the CTO. Key constraints:

- We will be handling PHI in a subset of flows (document redaction + triage) so data residency and isolation are mandatory.
- Target pilot: ~1k monthly active reporters, average 3 sessions/day, peak concurrency ~60–80 requests/min. Typical payloads ~800 tokens input / 1200 tokens output (so long tail exists).
- SLA expectation for pilot: 200ms median token latency for chat; burst capacity for reports around end-of-month.
- Procurement timeline: vendor evaluation in 4 weeks; contract execution ~8–10 weeks after approval.

Attached is the RFP excerpt with the compliance checklist. We need: (a) a conservative capacity plan with assumptions; (b) a rough TCO delta (monthly) for Dedicated vs Private; (c) an implementation timeline and blockers (procurement/lead times).

Can you send a short comparison and a mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday? Procurement will want something they can circulate.

Thanks,
Ellen Sullivan
Director, Platform Engineering
MedSafe Corp

Ellen — appreciate the clear ask and RFP. High-level answers below; attaching a working spreadsheet with assumptions and per-model perf numbers (medsafe_initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx). I kept this intentionally conservative for procurement.

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended approach: start with Dedicated reserved baseline + optional Private nodes for PHI-sensitive routes. This hybrid minimizes procurement lead time while meeting strict isolation for PHI.
- Ballpark monthly delta (Dedicated baseline vs Private full isolation): Dedicated baseline ~ $48k/mo; Private full ~ $135k/mo (includes hardware depreciation, on-prem network egress, and support). Exacts depend on model choice and quantization.

Sizing assumptions used (see sheet):
- Workload: 80 peak reqs/min, average 45 reqs/min; mean input+output tokens = 2000 tokens/req; token generation rate ~50 tokens/sec per model instance during generation.
- Model: we recommend using a quantized Llama-variant for cost-sensitive paths and an FP16-optimized 70B variant for the high-quality PHI pipeline.

Option A — Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated, single-tenant pool):
- Baseline: 8 x c4-standard L4-class inference nodes (L4-like performance) for interactive, plus 4 x H100-80GB for heavy PHI model variants during the pilot peak (can be reserved).
- Effective concurrency: ~140 concurrent generation slots across the pool (assuming batching and KV cache for chat); estimated 220k tokens/min throughput.
- Autoscaling: fast (seconds) within pool; fallback policy to smaller model variants if exhausted.
- Pros: fastest onboarding (2–4 weeks), Redwood-managed ops, cost-effective for mixed workloads (no capital).
- Cons: logically multi-tenant control plane (but dedicated compute), requires contractual SLA addendum for PHI handling and encryption keys.

Option B — Private (VPC / customer-managed or on-prem isolated deployment):
- Baseline: 16 x H100-80GB equivalent nodes (or 24 x A100-80GB if H100 procurement is slow) sized to cover the same throughput with headroom and cold-starts; includes on-prem infra costs and KMS/HSM integration.
- Effective concurrency: ~300 concurrent slots (more headroom, better for big-batch offline jobs).
- Procurement/lead time: hardware + install + network validation — conservative 10–16 weeks; add 2–3 weeks for KMS and audit evidence collection.
- Pros: full isolation, customer has direct hardware control and audit trail for PHI; can meet stricter legal/insurance requirements.
- Cons: capital expense, longer time-to-value, requires internal ops resources or Redwood Private support contract.

Implementation timeline (pilot):
- Week 0–2: contract & SOW sign (Dedicated can be first); procurement kickoff for Private in parallel.
- Week 2–6: Dedicated pool provisioning, model load and SLO tests, canary traffic (opt-in).
- Week 8–14: Private hardware delivery + on-site install or VPC validation; security attestation and SOC evidence collection.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick internal call Tues/Wed to align on model variants and which endpoints must be Private vs Dedicated.
2) We'll share the spreadsheet with per-GPU numeric costing and a short mutual action plan for procurement (DocuSign-ready).
3) If you confirm we should pursue hybrid, we can lock the Dedicated reserve to meet your 90-day canary.

Attaching: medsafe_initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx

Soojin / Ellen — quick engineering notes from my side after reviewing the spreadsheet:

- KV-cache warmup: for PHI-sensitive flows we cannot rely on long-lived public caches. Plan includes a priming period; recommend a short pre-warm job during off-peak to populate caches for common prefixes. That ups initial capacity needs by ~15% for first 48 hours.
- Model cold-starts: Private hardware will need pre-warming strategy; add reserved slot headroom in the Private plan (I accounted for this in the attached workbook).
- Autoscaling delta: Dedicated autoscaling is faster (because routers can drop into idle GPU pools) — Private autoscale is limited by procurement/VM/node spin-up unless you use a hybrid of reserved standby nodes.
- Procurement lead time risk: Suppliers are currently quoting 10–14 weeks for H100 and ~6–8 weeks for A100; if procurement is on the critical path we should consider a mixed GPU fleet (e.g., baseline A100s + a few H100s for peak accuracy) to shorten delivery time.

Operational ask for MedSafe: please identify which API endpoints will carry PHI. If we can reduce the PHI surface to a single route (eg: /redact + /triage), it simplifies the Private-only footprint and lowers cost.

I'll add a tab to the workbook showing two alternative mixes (A100-primary vs H100-primary) with estimated lead times and cost impact.

— Rishi
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
